l4_steps.name: Receive and log charter inquiry in CRM
l4_steps.input: Inbound charter enquiry via email, broker portal, or direct call
l4_steps.output: Charter opportunity record with client, route, date, and pax count
l4_steps.kpi: Inquiry-to-quote response time ≤4 hours for Group >50 pax
l4_steps.pain_point: Unstructured enquiry intake (email/phone) causes data loss and delays; no dedicated charter request portal integrated with Salesforce

l4_steps.name: Validate client credit standing and compliance
l4_steps.input: Client entity name and billing details from opportunity record
l4_steps.output: Credit risk tier (Low / Medium / High) and compliance clearance flag
l4_steps.kpi: Credit check completed within 2 hours of inquiry receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual credit verification via third-party tools not embedded in Salesforce; repeat credit checks for known clients due to lack of CRM integration

l4_steps.name: Check aircraft and crew availability in schedule
l4_steps.input: Requested departure date, route, and aircraft type from CRM opportunity
l4_steps.output: Available tail numbers and crew pairing windows for requested date
l4_steps.kpi: Availability check completed within 1 business hour; fleet utilisation conflict rate <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter requests compete with scheduled service rotations; SkyWORKS schedule locks can prevent real-time availability reads during peak planning cycles

l4_steps.name: Calculate block-hour cost and fuel uplift estimate
l4_steps.input: Route distance (nautical miles), aircraft type, block hours, fuel price index
l4_steps.output: Direct operating cost estimate (fuel, crew, overflight fees, handling)
l4_steps.kpi: Cost model accuracy vs actuals ≤5% variance on completed charters
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus NRM is O&D-optimised for scheduled service; charter block-hour cost models are maintained in offline Excel workbooks outside the RM system, creating version control risk

l4_steps.name: Assess displaced scheduled revenue opportunity cost
l4_steps.input: Requested aircraft and dates, scheduled service forecast for same rotation
l4_steps.output: Opportunity cost figure (displaced revenue from scheduled pax) and net charter value
l4_steps.kpi: Charter net margin ≥15% above displaced scheduled service yield
l4_steps.pain_point: Displaced revenue calculation requires manual extraction of RM forecast data; no automated what-if tool to compare charter vs scheduled revenue in real time

l4_steps.name: Obtain Revenue Management approval for charter pricing
l4_steps.input: Block-hour cost estimate and displaced revenue opportunity cost
l4_steps.output: Approved floor price, target price, and negotiation band for the charter
l4_steps.kpi: RM approval turnaround ≤4 hours; pricing approval SLA breach rate <10%
l4_steps.pain_point: No formal workflow routing for charter pricing approvals in Amadeus NRM; approvals handled via email, creating audit trail gaps for regulatory and financial compliance

l4_steps.name: Build and transmit formal charter proposal to client
l4_steps.input: Approved pricing band, route details, aircraft type, and service inclusions
l4_steps.output: Charter proposal document (PDF) with pricing, terms, validity period, and deposit schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal issued within 6 hours of RM approval; proposal acceptance rate ≥40%
l4_steps.pain_point: Proposal templates are maintained outside Salesforce; manual formatting increases turnaround time and introduces inconsistency across sales reps

l4_steps.name: Negotiate charter terms and revise pricing if needed
l4_steps.input: Client counter-proposal or revision request against issued proposal
l4_steps.output: Revised proposal within approved negotiation band or escalation to RM for exception
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation rounds ≤3 before agreement or rejection; average deal close time ≤5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Negotiation iterations not tracked in CRM opportunity stages; pricing concessions granted below floor price without RM visibility due to lack of automated guardrails

l4_steps.name: Generate charter contract from approved terms
l4_steps.input: Agreed pricing, route, date, pax count, service level, and penalty clauses
l4_steps.output: Executed charter contract with digital signatures from airline and client
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution within 24 hours of verbal agreement; contract error rate <2%
l4_steps.pain_point: DocuSign not integrated with Salesforce CRM; contract data entry is manual, risking discrepancies between CRM opportunity record and signed contract terms

l4_steps.name: Collect deposit payment and record in receivables
l4_steps.input: Executed contract with deposit amount and due date
l4_steps.output: Deposit receipt posted to charter receivables ledger; booking confirmed in CRM
l4_steps.kpi: Deposit received within 5 business days of contract execution; deposit collection rate ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated dunning workflow for charter deposit collection in SAP; manual follow-up required, and overdue deposits are not automatically flagged in Salesforce CRM

l4_steps.name: Apply for overflight and landing permits
l4_steps.input: Confirmed route, registration, date, and flight number from executed contract
l4_steps.output: Permit applications submitted to relevant CAAs and overflight authorities
l4_steps.kpi: Permit applications filed ≥10 days before departure for international routes; permit clearance rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Permit processing times vary by country (24 hours to 10+ days); no centralised permit tracking system — status monitored via email chains with handling agents, risking missed deadlines

l4_steps.name: File flight plan and request airport slots
l4_steps.input: Approved permits, route, and aircraft registration
l4_steps.output: Confirmed slot times at origin and destination airports; SSIM slot entry in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.kpi: Slot confirmed ≥5 days before departure; slot change rate <10% post-confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter flights at slot-coordinated airports (IATA Level 3) compete with scheduled carriers; last-minute charter requests are often rejected, requiring costly alternative routing

l4_steps.name: Assign crew pairing and verify duty-time compliance
l4_steps.input: Confirmed flight date, departure time, route, and block hours
l4_steps.output: Crew pairing with duty-time compliance verification per FAR Part 117
l4_steps.kpi: Crew assigned ≥72 hours before departure; FAR Part 117 violation rate = 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter dates often conflict with scheduled crew pairings; Jeppesen requires manual pairing creation for ad-hoc charters, and duty-time buffers may be exhausted if schedule disruptions precede the charter

l4_steps.name: Coordinate fuel uplift, catering, and ground handling
l4_steps.input: Aircraft type, pax count, catering specification, and station identifiers
l4_steps.output: Ground services order confirmation at origin and destination stations
l4_steps.kpi: Ground handling confirmed ≥48 hours before departure; catering order accuracy ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter stations may be uncontracted airports; negotiating ad-hoc fuel and handling rates increases cost unpredictability and erodes the charter margin estimated in Phase 2

l4_steps.name: Execute charter flight and record departure/arrival actuals
l4_steps.input: Confirmed crew pairing, flight plan, slot time, and pax manifest
l4_steps.output: Actual departure/arrival times, block hours flown, and pax count recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Charter on-time departure (D0) ≥85%; pax manifest discrepancy rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter pax manifests are often finalised late by clients; last-minute pax additions or removals require real-time weight & balance recalculations, delaying departure

l4_steps.name: Capture actual costs and reconcile against estimate
l4_steps.input: Actual fuel receipts, handling invoices, permit fees, and crew actuals
l4_steps.output: Variance report: actual cost vs pre-flight estimate with margin impact
l4_steps.kpi: Cost reconciliation completed within 5 business days of flight; cost variance ≤8% of estimate
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel and handling invoices from ad-hoc stations arrive weeks after the flight; SAP posting cutoffs create accrual uncertainty, requiring manual re-opening of periods for charter settlements

l4_steps.name: Issue final invoice and collect balance payment
l4_steps.input: Actual cost report, contract price, deposit received, and any agreed extras
l4_steps.output: Final tax invoice issued; balance payment collected and posted to charter revenue account
l4_steps.kpi: Final invoice issued within 7 business days of flight; payment collected within contract terms (net 14 days); DSO for charter ≤21 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Client disputes over fuel surcharges or extras delay final payment; no automated dispute escalation workflow in SAP, requiring manual intervention by Finance and Sales teams

l4_steps.name: Conduct post-charter debrief and update client record
l4_steps.input: Client satisfaction feedback, operations debrief notes, and final financial result
l4_steps.output: Closed opportunity record with win/loss analysis, margin achieved, and repeat-sale flag
l4_steps.kpi: Debrief completed within 10 business days of flight; repeat charter conversion rate ≥30%
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-charter learnings (pricing accuracy, permit delays, ground handling issues) are not systematically fed back into pricing models or permit planning checklists, causing repeated errors
